# Harness Summary

The harness achieves moderate evaluation accuracy (62–63%) but exhibits poor training performance (40–51%), revealing failure to effectively learn from provided in-context examples. The dominant failure pattern is selecting labels that appear in the demonstrations rather than learning the underlying classification rule; reasoning shows no meaningful variation across different inputs. Systematic confusions between specific label pairs suggest the model defaults to nearby demonstration labels when uncertain rather than genuinely reasoning about problem content. Critically, reasoning remains shallow throughout evaluation with no evidence of learning progression, indicating the harness does not enable semantic pattern internalization. To improve, prioritize demonstration selection that clearly separates competing labels, add explicit anchors highlighting distinguishing features, and redesign prompts to force deeper reasoning beyond surface-level pattern matching.
